A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find the IGM to be consistent with enrichment by a population of early stars, with the caveat that we cannot rule out the possibility of significant enrichment from Ly-break galaxies.

the current observational data is consistent with the idea of early enrichment by Population III (Pop III) stars and objects, and that there may be a contribution from late enrichment by Pop II galaxies.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGM is a powerful probe of the early Universe and that the combination of the ‘pixel optical depths’, QSO spectra, and simulations is a powerful tool for understanding the early Universe.

the observed carbon abundances are consistent with a picture of early enrichment by the first galaxies, while the observed silicon abundances are consistent only with a picture of late enrichment by $2\lesssim z \lesssim 3$ galaxies.

there is currently no evidence for a significant contribution to the IGM from early enrichment, and that the IGM abundances can be explained by late enrichment by $z \lesssim 6$ Ly-break galaxies, although we caution that there are many uncertainties that remain in the modelling of intergalactic abundances.
